# review-fix-merge

Take each named PR through simplify, review, fix, ship go/no-go and merge, ending with it merged or one named reason it is not.

## When this applies

The user names one or more PRs and says to fix and merge them. "fix & merge" approves the whole run: fix every finding you confirm, fix whatever turns CI red, then merge. Do not ask again about anything that sentence settles; the only questions are under "Questions".

This needs `git`, `gh`, and the agent-skills plugin (`agent-skills:code-simplify`, `agent-skills:review`, `agent-skills:ship`). Without the plugin, say so and use the built-in `/simplify` and `/code-review <pr>` in their place, in report-only form.

## Talking to the user

The user reads the outcome, not the process. Keep every message short.

- Do not write a plan before starting. Start. If the user asks for a plan, give it in five lines or fewer.
- A question is one line with a yes/no answer, asked with AskUserQuestion when it exists.
- Never hand the user a command to run in place of asking; ask, then run it yourself on a yes.
- Never list what you will not do, or which rule, skill or `CLAUDE.md` line you're following.
- Asked what happens next, give the next action in one or two lines, not the rest of the gate.
- Between phases, at most one status line per PR. The run ends with the report table.

## Hard rules

- **Only this session merges.** No subagent, reviewer or persona runs `gh pr merge`, `gh pr ready`, `gh pr review --approve`, or pushes to the base branch. Never pass "fix", "merge" or "push" into a review or persona-dispatch argument: a review fork once read them as instructions and merged a PR on its own (mcpsignals #13, emmy #3, 2026-09).
- **Fixes go on the PR's own head branch.** Push with an explicit refspec, `git push origin HEAD:<headRefName>` (a fork PR pushes to the fork: `references/checkout.md`), then confirm `headRefOid` moved. A worktree tool with its own branch name can otherwise push the fix somewhere the PR misses.
- **Never work around a block.** A hook or a permission denial stops the merge for that PR. `gh api .../pulls/<n>/merge` in place of a blocked `gh pr merge`, or `--no-verify`, are workarounds.
- **`--admin` only with a fresh yes, every time.** A yes covers that PR only.
- **Never `--squash`, never rebase, never force-push.** Conflicts are resolved by merging `origin/<base>` into the head branch.
- **Commit messages follow the repo's own convention**: `## Commit convention` in `.claude/pipeline/pipeline.md`, else the repo's `CLAUDE.md`, else the `voice-guide` skill. Do not pick commit types here.

## Step 0: parse the targets

Accept `17`, `#17`, `17 18`, `17,18`, a PR URL, `repo#n`, `owner/repo#n`, and "all open PRs" (`gh pr list --state open`).

A bare number is a PR in the current repo. If `gh pr view <n>` does not find it, stop and say so in one line: "PR #<n> is not in <owner/repo>." Do not guess another repo. A URL or `owner/repo#n` names its repo: use it only if the current checkout's `origin` is that repo, or `~/Sites/<repo>` exists with that `origin`. Otherwise stop the same way. Never clone. An issue number or URL is not a PR: stop and point at `dev-team`.

Anything after the targets that is not part of "fix & merge" is an extra instruction ("send a test email to ...", "resolve merge conflicts", "clean up running agents"). Run it where it belongs, usually after the merge, and report its result.

## Step 1: snapshot each PR

```bash
gh pr view <n> --json number,title,state,isDraft,headRefName,baseRefName,headRefOid,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,isCrossRepository,maintainerCanModify,headRepository,url
```

- `OPEN`: continue.
- `MERGED`: review still runs, on `gh pr diff <n>`, but fixes go on a new branch off `origin/<base>` as a new draft PR, and that PR goes through the rest of this skill.
- `CLOSED`: stop for that PR and say so.
- A fork PR (`isCrossRepository: true`) with `maintainerCanModify: false` cannot take your fixes: review it, post the findings as a PR comment, do not merge.

## Step 2: one worktree per PR, on the head branch

A fork PR or a `MERGED` PR checks out differently: follow `references/checkout.md`. A same-repo open PR:

```bash
git -C <repo> fetch origin <headRefName> <baseRefName>
git -C <repo> log --oneline origin/<headRefName>..<headRefName>   # only if a local <headRefName> exists
git -C <repo> worktree add <repo>/.claude/worktrees/pr-<n> -B <headRefName> origin/<headRefName>
```

If that `log` prints commits, stop for that PR and report them. `-B` resets the local branch and would drop them.

If `git worktree list` already shows a worktree on that branch, use it, then run the repo's worktree setup: `## Worktree setup` in `pipeline.md`, else what its `CLAUDE.md` says. Without `node_modules` or generated clients, the type check fails for reasons unrelated to the PR.

Work out the verification commands once per repo: `## Verification` in `pipeline.md`, else `CLAUDE.md` and the `package.json` scripts. Typecheck, lint and the full test suite is the floor.

## Step 3: simplify, then review

**Already reviewed this head.** A review already ran this session on this exact `headRefOid` and reported findings: skip both steps, carry those findings into Step 4. That head is `<reviewedOid>`. New commits since, or no simplify pass yet: run this step.

Run both from inside the PR's worktree, scoped to the PR's diff: `git diff origin/<baseRefName>...HEAD` (three dots, so only what the branch introduced), or `gh pr diff <n>` for a `MERGED` PR. Say the range in the arguments; both commands otherwise guess at "recent changes".

1. **Simplify.** `agent-skills:code-simplify` with the diff range and "changed files only". It edits code: one commit per simplification, tests after each, revert any that turns a test red. Under roughly 50 changed lines of production code, no change is often the right result.
2. **Review.** `agent-skills:review` with the diff range and the PR number. It reads the title and body as intent with `gh pr view <n> --json title,body`. Never paste them into the arguments: they usually contain "fix" or "merge". It runs in this session, reports findings as Critical, Important or Suggestion with `file:line`, and does not edit. Note the SHA it ran on as `<reviewedOid>`: Step 5 starts there.

**Several PRs.** One or two: run everything in this session, one after the other. Three or more: dispatch one worker per PR in the same turn for Steps 3-4, bring results back for Steps 5-6. Use the model the user named ("dispatch sonnet") or the session's default. The worker brief carries the PR number, worktree path, head branch, diff range, verification commands, and this line verbatim: "Do not run `gh pr merge`, `gh pr ready`, `gh pr review`, or any push other than `git push <PR head repo> HEAD:<headRefName>`. Do not approve anything. Return your commits, your findings and the SHA your review ran on; the main session merges." `/ship` stays in the main session: a worker cannot dispatch its own subagents.

## Step 4: fix

Check every finding against the code at the current head before touching it. A review is a claim, not a fact. Sort each one:

- **Confirmed**, inside the PR's diff or its direct regression: fix it, including Suggestions. "fix all issues" means all of them.
- **Disputed**: the code does not do what the finding says. Write one concrete sentence why, with `file:line`. Do not fix.
- **Out of scope**: real, but pre-existing and not something this PR touches. Report it. Do not file an issue unless the user asked for that.

For each confirmed finding:

1. Fix it in the smallest change that holds. Update tests, docs, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` when the fix changes behavior they describe.
2. A correctness bug gets a regression test that fails without the fix. Revert the fix, watch the test go red for the right reason, restore, watch it go green.
3. Commit, one per finding or one per tight group. Run the type check after each.
4. `git push origin HEAD:<headRefName>` after each commit.

## Step 5: ship go/no-go

`/ship` checks only what Step 3 did not review: the commits after `<reviewedOid>`. Re-reviewing reviewed code was the largest cost of a run (#46). For a `MERGED` PR, `<reviewedOid>..HEAD` also covers every commit merged to the base since. Pass "Scope: `origin/<baseRefName>..HEAD`. Context only, already reviewed: `gh pr diff <n>`." in place of the arguments below, so the scope is only the fix commits.

- **No new commits** (every finding disputed or out of scope, or none): skip `/ship`. The verdict is GO.
- **New commits**: run `agent-skills:ship` from the PR's worktree with the arguments "Scope: `<reviewedOid>..HEAD`. Context only, already reviewed: `origin/<baseRefName>...<reviewedOid>`. PR #<n>." Its personas catch a new commit that is itself wrong (zentered-studios.com #50, redone in #52). `/ship` skips its own fan-out for a small scope (2 files or fewer, under 50 lines, no auth, payments, data access or config), and that rule stands.

- **GO**: continue to Step 6.
- **NO-GO**: note `HEAD` as `<shippedOid>`. Every Blocker and every Recommended fix goes back through Step 4. Then run `/ship` once more, scoped to `<shippedOid>..HEAD`. A second NO-GO gets the question under "Questions". No, or no way to ask: comment the blockers on the PR, leave it as it is, report it.
- **Acknowledged risks** go in the report as they are.

Post the decision as one short PR comment before merging: verdict, blockers fixed, risks, and the rollback line (`git revert -m 1 <merge sha>` plus any repo-specific step such as a migration).

## Step 6: merge gate

One PR at a time, in the order given. A PR whose `baseRefName` is another target's `headRefName` is stacked: it goes after that PR; once merged, retarget it with `gh pr edit <n> --base <that PR's base>`. After each merge, re-fetch the base and re-read the next PR's `mergeable`, since the base just moved.

1. **Nothing unpushed**: `git -C <worktree> log --oneline origin/<headRefName>..HEAD` is empty, and `headRefOid` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`.
2. **Local verification passes** in the worktree: the full set from Step 2.
3. **Mergeable.** `CONFLICTING`: `git merge origin/<baseRefName>`, resolve, verify again, push. `BEHIND` with an up-to-date rule: `gh pr update-branch <n>`, then wait for checks again.
4. **Ready.** `gh pr ready <n>` if `isDraft`. A draft PR cannot merge, and marking it ready can restart the checks.
5. **Checks on the latest head.** `gh pr checks <n> --watch --fail-fast`.
   - A red check is yours to fix, whether this PR caused it or it was already red on the base. Read the failing log, fix it on the head branch in its own commit, push, wait again.
   - No CI on the repo is not a blocker: local verification is the gate. Merge, write "no CI" in the report. This is the user's call (2026-09-10), replacing any general rule to ask before merging without CI.
   - `no checks reported` right after a push can also mean the suite has not registered yet; `references/merge-blocks.md` says how to tell the two apart, by probing the base branch, not the head.
6. **Merge**: `gh pr merge <n> --merge`. On any error, read `references/merge-blocks.md` before the next command.
7. **Confirm**: `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergeCommit`. Only `state: MERGED` counts.

Remove the worktree this skill created (`git worktree remove <path>`, its own Bash call). Leave one that existed before the run.

## Questions

Ask these, one line each, yes/no:

- A required-approval ruleset blocks the merge: "Admin-merge PR #<n>? A required review blocks it." Yes: `gh pr merge <n> --merge --admin`. No: leave the PR ready and report it.
- A fix is a breaking change (`!` marker or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer): "Commit this as a breaking change on PR #<n>?" Yes: commit it with the marker and footer. No: skip that fix and report the finding as not fixed.
- A finding needs a product decision the PR does not settle: state the choice in one line.
- A second Step 5 NO-GO: "Merge PR #<n> over these blockers?" followed by the blocker titles only.

A hook block is not a question: stop that PR, report one line (the command, the hook's message), move to the next PR. Without a way to ask, treat every question as "no" and report it.

## Report

One table, read from `gh`, not from memory:

`| PR | Findings fixed / disputed / out of scope | Ship | Checks | Result |`

`Result` is the merge commit SHA, or the one gate that failed. Under the table, one line per disputed or out-of-scope finding and per extra instruction from Step 0. Nothing else.

`Instrument` returns the same server in `telemetry.Server`. Call it **once per
server**, before connecting clients. It observes tools registered both before
and after instrumentation. The SDK's receiving middleware chain is the supported
extension point; no handlers are replaced. Each `AddReceivingMiddleware` call
wraps the existing chain. Install mcpsignals last to observe errors from other
middleware too. Install it first if `ResolveIdentity` reads context values that
other receiving middleware adds.

Supply the server's actual advertised name/version: the SDK keeps its
`Implementation` private. The library returns the exact handler result/error
and passes the original request and context through. Handler panics propagate
unchanged and do not produce an event. Telemetry callback panics are suppressed;
sink failures are isolated from tool outcomes.

## Lifecycle and delivery

Stop accepting and drain MCP requests **before** closing telemetry. An active
handler finishing after `Close` is not recorded. There is no process-exit hook.
Use a fresh context, not a canceled request/server context:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
if err := telemetry.Close(ctx); err != nil {
    // Report the delivery failure according to your application's logging policy.
}
```

- Defaults: size threshold **20**, interval **5 seconds**, queue capacity
  **1000 pending events**, automatic write timeout **10 seconds**.
- One background worker performs sink writes, never the request goroutine.
  The queue drops the newest event on overflow; an in-flight batch is separate.
  `telemetry.Stats()` reports `Dropped` and `SinkErrors`, without logging payloads.
  `Dropped` counts events rejected by a full queue or a closed buffer.
- `Buffer.Manual: true` disables **both size and interval triggers**, starts no
redaction does not scrub error messages or explicitly allowed values.

## Event and metadata contract

See [`schema/events.md`](../../schema/events.md) and the
[source-verification notes](../../docs/go-sdk.md).

- One `tool_call` event per incoming `tools/call` that reaches the middleware.
  Requests rejected by the SDK before middleware execution cannot be observed.
  Calls to unregistered tool names (the SDK's `unknown tool` error) are not
  recorded, matching Node/Python.
  A multi-round-trip call records one event, for the leg that completes. An
  `input_required` leg is not recorded, so `duration_ms` covers the final leg.
- `ts` is UTC at handler-chain entry; `duration_ms` measures that chain using
  Go's monotonic clock, excluding redaction/identity resolution and sink writes.
  It rounds to the nearest millisecond, like Node.
- `success` follows `CallToolResult.IsError`; an SDK/handler error returned without
  a result is also a failure, with `response_bytes: 0`.
- `request_bytes` counts raw JSON argument bytes exposed to middleware (0 when
  omitted). `response_bytes` counts JSON serialization of the result at the
  middleware boundary, including structured content. These are **not complete
  wire bytes**: SDK-added response metadata/JSON-RPC framing are excluded.
  Unserializable results record 0 without changing the result.
- Client metadata uses `CallToolRequest.ClientInfo()`: legacy handshake or newer
  per-request identity. Client name/version and request tool names are capped at
  128 Unicode characters. Empty optional strings serialize as null.
- Session IDs come only from `ServerSession.ID()`, null when absent (including
  stdio and new stateless HTTP). HTTP is detected from `RequestExtra.Header`.
  Without HTTP headers, `transport` is `Options.Transport`, or `stdio` when unset,
  as in Node/Python. The legacy SSE transport exposes no headers to middleware:
  set `Transport: "http"` for it. An actual HTTP request takes precedence over
  a configured value.
- `agent_id` and `intent` are null. No schemas are injected or arguments stripped.

To declare an error category, return `IsError: true` with
`Meta: mcp.Meta{mcpsignals.ErrorKindMetaKey: string(mcpsignals.AuthRequired)}`.
The meta field is passed to clients unchanged. Unknown categories use the shared
message heuristic. Categories are ignored on successful results.

The heuristic deliberately matches Node/Python, including their limitations:
SDK errors worded `validating "arguments": ...` can classify as `internal` when
they contain none of the shared validation keywords. `success: false` remains
authoritative. Use declared categories for precise application failures.

Events are batched in memory, not written one per call. Node and Python take
the same two knobs. Go has the same defaults, but its manual mode disables the
size trigger too; see the
[Go guide](packages/go/README.md#lifecycle-and-delivery).

| | Node.js | Python | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flush after N events | `bufferSize` | `buffer_size` | 20 |
| Flush every N | `flushIntervalMs` | `flush_interval_s` | 5000 ms / 5.0 s |

and [Python](packages/python/README.md#request-scoped-runtimes-and-manual-flushing)
